children: , the advanced-chipmaking equipment giant, broke ground Tuesday on a 35-hectare campus designed to relieve its increasingly tight EUV production pipeline. The stock climbed approximately 2% to $1,751.66 as investors welcomed another aggressive bet on sustained semiconductor demand.

The company's construction update places the first opening in 2029, when the site should accommodate at least 3,000 employees. If fully developed, the Eindhoven campus could eventually provide 20,000 workplaces across 350,000 square meters. Its centerpiece will be a new flow factory bringing TWINSCAN materials, manufacturing and installation operations under one roof.

ASML shipped 86 new lithography systems in the second quarter, a 28.4% jump from the first quarter, while management is already targeting a 30% increase in low-NA EUV capacity for 2027. The chart captures the valuation pressure surrounding that growth story: ASML's $1,751.66 price sits 40.87% above its GF Value estimate of roughly $1,240. The campus strengthens the long-term capacity argument, but it will not open soon enough to solve today's bottleneckexisting plants and suppliers must still carry three more years of customer commitments.

title: ASML Climbs as a 35-Hectare Factory Targets Its Bottleneck
